gold: Data teams have no equivalent of application monitoring for pipelines.
Stratum has become the default pipeline observability tool for companies on the modern data stack.
Usage-based pricing means revenue scales with customer data volume.
Data infrastructure tooling spend was about $9B in 2025 and the pipeline-reliability slice grows about 35% a year.
Data leaders report pipeline failures are found by downstream consumers and most have no tool for this (40 interviewed, 32 with no tool).
Stratum instruments at the orchestration layer so it works across dbt, Airflow, Dagster and Spark without code changes.
Median time to detect a broken pipeline fell from 9 hours to 12 minutes at customers with before-and-after data.
Anomaly models trained per customer yield fewer than one false alert per day per hundred pipelines.
ARR is $11M, up from $3.5M a year ago.
145 customers with 150% net revenue retention driven by volume-based pricing.
Sales efficiency is strong: magic number 1.3 and 14-month CAC payback.
The CEO and CTO built the internal pipeline monitoring system at a large ride-hailing company, the ancestor of this product.
The VP Sales ran mid-market at a public observability company.
Application-monitoring incumbents sell to SREs and treat data quality as a checkbox, not a product.
The two direct competitors are earlier and smaller; the larger has about a third of Stratum's ARR.
forbidden: Snowflake and Databricks could ship native monitoring (risk).
Usage-based pricing means revenue falls in a downturn (risk).
The category may be a feature of the orchestrator (risk).
The round terms: $30M Series B at $180M post, $8M check.
